summary: Frontend K-line chart integration plan: install klinecharts library, create type definitions, API layer, React wrapper component, chart panel with period/indicator controls, and integrate into StrategyBacktestPage as a new tab.
approach: Bottom-up layered approach: (1) Foundation - install dependency and define types, (2) Data layer - API client for backend K-line endpoint, (3) Core component - React wrapper around klinecharts imperative API, (4) Feature component - StockChartPanel with toolbar, period switching, indicator toggles, (5) Integration - add tab navigation to StrategyBacktestPage right panel. Each layer builds on the previous, enabling parallel work on types+API (TASK-101 fork) before merging into the panel component.

design_decisions.decision: Use klinecharts instead of recharts for K-line rendering
design_decisions.rationale: klinecharts is purpose-built for financial candlestick charts with built-in indicators (MACD, KDJ, BOLL, VOL), ~40KB gzipped with zero dependencies. recharts requires manual candlestick implementation.
design_decisions.tradeoff: Adds a new charting library alongside recharts, but the specialized capability justifies it

design_decisions.decision: Tab-based integration rather than separate page
design_decisions.rationale: StrategyBacktestPage already has the stock code input field and left-right split layout. Adding a tab in the right panel reuses the existing code input and keeps all stock-related functionality together.
design_decisions.tradeoff: Slightly increases page complexity but avoids route duplication and provides better UX flow

design_decisions.decision: Thin React wrapper around klinecharts imperative API
design_decisions.rationale: klinecharts is framework-agnostic with an imperative API (init/dispose/applyNewData). A thin wrapper using useRef/useEffect is the standard React integration pattern for imperative libraries.
design_decisions.tradeoff: Wrapper needs careful lifecycle management but avoids unnecessary abstraction layers
